correctness.rationale: The adjacency Hamiltonian splits orthogonally into antisymmetric -1, symmetric +1, and a two-dimensional hub sector with eigenvalues (1±sqrt(8m+1))/2. Their propagators yield the exact amplitude. Nonzero positive eigenprojection weights force an incompatible eigenphase product for any putative PGST sequence. A sharp localization bound restricts optimal times to O(m^-1/2) windows, a two-torus density argument gives the nonsquare coefficient, and a compact rescaling with a uniformly strictly concave single-variable objective gives the two square-frequency subsequences. Actual companion matrix-exp checks corroborate 168 instances but are not the proof.

value.rationale: Quantifies a natural best-possible quantum communication probability within a triangle motif embedded in a growing common-hub network. The leading optimal infidelity, despite convergence to perfect transfer with network size, changes discontinuously between irrational and two integer-frequency residue families. The computed constants explain how exact spectral commensurability penalizes transfer and distinguish finite-time recurrence physics from global time averages.
